claims.explanation: Mitoxantrone is a topoisomerase II poison whose cytotoxicity is limited by drug efflux via ABCG2/BCRP; thus lines with low ABCG2 expression and intact p53-mediated DNA-damage apoptosis are most sensitive, while high ABCG2 expression or loss of p53/CD95 signaling confers resistance. The selective killing pattern is best explained by ABCG2 expression as the dominant protective feature, with TP53 mutation and DNA-repair/efflux pathway alterations modulating response.

features.basis: BCRP/ABCG2 overexpression confers mitoxantrone resistance via ATP-dependent efflux (PMID 9861027, 14576842, 15381773)
p53 is required for CD95 receptor upregulation and apoptosis after mitoxantrone-induced DNA damage; loss reduces sensitivity (PMID 9841917)
TOP2A is the direct target of mitoxantrone; higher expression increases poison-induced cleavage complexes (PMID 20534341)
ABCA3 is co-expressed with ABCG2 in drug-efflux-high side population cells that survive mitoxantrone (PMID 15381773)
CD95/Fas receptor upregulation is p53-dependent and mediates apoptosis after mitoxantrone treatment (PMID 9841917)
FBXW7-mutant lines are enriched among the most killed lines, possibly via impaired DNA-damage response or mitotic checkpoint control
ATM-mutant lines appear among the most killed, consistent with defective DNA-damage repair increasing topoisomerase-poison cytotoxicity
PTEN loss is enriched in sensitive lines, possibly through impaired DNA repair and increased replication stress
ARID1A mutations appear in several highly killed lines, suggesting chromatin-remodeling defects enhance sensitivity
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are among the most killed, possibly reflecting MAPK-driven proliferation dependence
EGFR-mutant lung lines are enriched in the sensitive group, possibly via oncogene-addicted proliferation
KRAS-mutant lines are enriched among the least affected, suggesting RAS-driven survival signaling reduces mitoxantrone sensitivity
